title: Alex Kidd in Miracle World
summary: Sega's mascot before Sonic, built right into the memory of the Tec Toy Master System. Rock, paper, scissors to settle the boss fights.

title: Mônica no Castelo do Dragão
summary: Tec Toy swapped Wonder Boy for Monica's Gang, Brazil's best-known comic strip kids, and made the most Brazilian adventure on the Master System. Her stuffed bunny Samson instead of a sword.

title: Phantasy Star
summary: A space RPG with first-person dungeons that looked like witchcraft in 1987. Plenty of people discovered the genre through the Tec Toy catalog.

title: Sonic the Hedgehog
summary: The 8-bit version that came built into so many consoles sold in Brazil. A slower Green Hill, but with all the charm of the first time.

title: Wonder Boy
summary: Run nonstop, eat fruit so your energy doesn't run out and throw the hatchet. Simple, addictive and in every home with a Master System.

title: Super Mario Bros.
summary: The game that taught the whole world to jump. In Brazil it ran on the Phantom System, the Dynavision and the Turbo Game, always on that thousand-in-one cartridge.

title: Contra
summary: Thirty lives from the secret code, two players on the couch and no survivors. The ultimate co-op shooter on the NES.

title: Mega Man 2
summary: Eight bosses, a timeless soundtrack and the dance of figuring out which weapon takes down whom.

title: Castlevania
summary: Whip in hand, treacherous stairs and the clock running all the way to Dracula. Hard the way the 80s liked it.

title: The Legend of Zelda
summary: The golden cartridge that invented exploring without a map. Good secrets got written down on a notebook page.

title: Pitfall!
summary: Vines, alligators and scorpions in twenty minutes racing the clock. The Atari icon in Brazilian living rooms.

title: River Raid
summary: Flying upriver, refueling at the right tank, never able to turn back. A high score was serious business at recess.

title: Enduro
summary: Passing cars from dawn to snowstorm, a whole day without taking your finger off the joystick button.

title: Metal Gear
summary: Solid Snake's debut, where hiding was worth more than shooting. It ran on the Gradiente and Sharp MSX computers that reached many Brazilian homes before any console did.

title: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
summary: Tails on your back, spin dash on the ground and Chemical Plant taking your breath away. The cartridge bundled with the Tec Toy Mega Drive.

title: Streets of Rage 2
summary: Axel, Blaze and a Yuzo Koshiro soundtrack that still plays in your head. Two-player beat 'em up until the lead pipe breaks.

title: Golden Axe
summary: A barbarian, a dwarf and an amazon riding a blue dragon. The magic potion always saved for the moment of despair.

title: Shining Force
summary: A tactical RPG where every step on the board is a life-or-death decision. The way into the genre for a lot of people.

title: Phantasy Star IV
summary: The end of the Algol saga, with comic panels on screen and team combos. An expensive cartridge, the dream of every rental store shelf.

title: Castle of Illusion Starring Mickey Mouse
summary: Mickey butt-bouncing against the witch Mizrabel, in stages that looked like a cartoon playing on the living room TV.

title: Mortal Kombat II
summary: Blood on without needing a code, and fatalities copied from a magazine page. It sparked arguments in every neighborhood rental store.

title: Super Mario World
summary: Yoshi, the yellow cape and ninety-six exits to find. The reason to rent a Super Nintendo for the whole weekend.

title: Donkey Kong Country
summary: Pre-rendered graphics that looked like magic in 1994, Diddy in the barrel and the water level with the prettiest music of the 16-bit era.

title: Top Gear
summary: Nitro counted on your fingers, split screen and that opening tune nobody forgets. The undisputed king of Brazilian rental stores.

title: Chrono Trigger
summary: Time travel, battles without a transition screen and a party you learn to love. An RPG that aged better than almost anything.

title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
summary: Hyrule and the Dark World as mirror images, with dungeons that teach without saying a word.

title: Super Metroid
summary: Samus alone on Zebes: the map opens up as you find the next ability. A silent lesson in level design.

title: Mega Man X
summary: Mega Man grew up: wall dash, hidden armor and Maverick bosses. The opening stage explains everything without a line of text.

title: Super Bomberman
summary: Four controllers, a cramped arena and friendship put to the test with every bomb. The official multiplayer of birthday parties.

title: Another World
summary: Science fiction in silent polygons, with no tutorial and no mercy. It felt more like a movie than a game.

title: Street Fighter II
summary: A coin left on top of the cabinet to call next. In Brazil, "hadouken" became part of everyday vocabulary.

title: Hard Drivin'
summary: A steering wheel that pushed back, a loop-the-loop and the crash replay playing for everyone to see. It was the most expensive token in the arcade and worth every cent.

title: Final Fight
summary: Haggar, Cody and Guy cleaning up Metro City with their fists. Every broken barrel hid a roast chicken.

title: Marvel vs. Capcom
summary: Ryu against Wolverine, assists jumping on screen and endless air combos. It was the loudest cabinet in the arcade.

title: Metal Slug
summary: Hand-drawn frame-by-frame animation, the little tank and the bearded hostages. Proof that the arcade Neo Geo played in another league.

title: The King of Fighters '97
summary: Teams of three, Iori against Kyo and the whole line waiting to challenge whoever was winning. The definitive KOF of Brazilian arcades.

title: Super Sidekicks 2
summary: Neo Geo soccer with excited commentary and bicycle kick goals. Brazil was already picked before the token even dropped.

title: Crash Bandicoot
summary: Running from the giant boulder, smashing crates and hearing that signature yell. The unofficial PlayStation mascot.

title: Resident Evil 2
summary: Raccoon City overrun, two scenarios that cross paths and heavy footsteps in the hallway. Horror that made you sleep with the bedroom light on.

title: Final Fantasy VII
summary: Midgar, Materia and a silver-haired villain. Three CDs that redefined how big an RPG could be.

title: Metal Gear Solid
summary: The Codec ringing, the radar blinking and a boss who read your memory card. Interactive cinema long before it was trendy.

title: Silent Hill
summary: The fog that hid the console's limits became the most psychological horror on the PS1. The radio static alone gave you chills.

title: Gran Turismo
summary: Earning your virtual license, filling the garage and watching the whole replay just for the pleasure of it. The sim that became a craze in Brazil.

title: Tekken 3
summary: Eddy Gordo spinning capoeira with the kick button mashed nonstop: the most popular Brazilian in 90s video games.

title: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night
summary: Alucard, the inverted castle and a chilling gothic soundtrack. The genre now called metroidvania was born here.

title: Super Mario 64
summary: The first triple jump in three dimensions. Still the definitive lesson in moving a character through space.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
summary: Hyrule Field wide open, Epona at a gallop and the ocarina bending time. It became the yardstick for every adventure that came after.

title: GoldenEye 007
summary: Four friends, split screen and the sacred rule of not peeking at someone else's corner. License to Kill mode was practically mandatory.

title: Ronaldinho Soccer 64
summary: The bootleg cartridge that swapped the Japanese teams for Brazilian soccer and showed up at every street vendor stall. A rough hack job, and we loved it.

title: Nights into Dreams
summary: Looping through dreamlike stages with Sega's analog controller. The Saturn had its gems too.

title: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City
summary: 80s neon, Hawaiian shirts and the radio tuned to the flashback station. Just driving around aimlessly was fun enough.

title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
summary: Three cities, bikes, the gym and cheat codes memorized by heart. It lived for years in the tray of many modded PS2s.

title: God of War
summary: Kratos and the Blades of Chaos against all of Olympus, with the right button showing up at the right time. The PS2 squeezed to the last drop.

title: Shadow of the Colossus
summary: Sixteen colossi, one horse and a world empty on purpose. Every climb ends with a bitter taste.

title: Devil May Cry
summary: A stylish Dante, the combo grade flashing on screen and the certainty that action could be elegant too.

title: Winning Eleven 9
summary: The soccer game that ruled the rental store and the street tournament: crisp passes, swapped player names and celebrations on the controller.

title: Bomba Patch
summary: The Brazilian fan patch that put the entire Brazilian league inside Winning Eleven, with local commentary and your team's crest. Sold at any newsstand.

title: Halo: Combat Evolved
summary: A giant ring, two weapons at a time and aiming that finally worked on a controller. It was the reason the first Xbox existed.

title: Shenmue
summary: Daily routine, winter weather and an unhurried investigation in Yokosuka. Too ambitious for its time, and unforgettable because of it.

title: Sonic Adventure
summary: Sonic in three dimensions racing through Station Square, with Chao to raise between stages. The Dreamcast debuting with energy to spare.

title: Resident Evil 4
summary: Over-the-shoulder camera, a hostile village and the sound of a chainsaw getting closer. It reinvented third-person action in one go.

title: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow
summary: Collecting each enemy's soul and building your own fighting style, all on the tiny Game Boy Advance screen.

title: Doom
summary: The 486 in the school computer lab could run it, the floppy went from hand to hand and the hallway became a battlefield. First-person shooting was born grown up.

title: Prince of Persia
summary: One hour on the clock, pixel-perfect jumps and unforgiving spikes. The rotoscoped animation seemed impossible for its time.

title: Halo 3
summary: The end of the trilogy, with a campaign to play as a duo and a multiplayer that kept the Xbox 360 on for years.

title: Dark Souls
summary: Lordran fitted together like clockwork, bonfires as a breather and the hard lesson of learning by dying.

title: The Last of Us
summary: Joel, Ellie and a journey that really hurts. The PS3 signing off with the most talked-about story of its generation.

title: Bloodborne
summary: Gothic Yharnam, aggression rewarded and a nightmare that changes shape with every discovery.

title: God of War
summary: Kratos as a father, the Leviathan Axe flying back to his hand and a camera without a single cut across the nine realms.

title: Marvel's Spider-Man
summary: Swinging through New York with the right rhythm is a complete thrill before the mission even starts.

title: Red Dead Redemption 2
summary: The Wild West coming to an end, with a camp that feels made of real people. Riding slowly is part of the charm.

title: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
summary: Katana duels to the beat of the deflect. Either you learn the enemy's posture, or you don't get past the bridge.

title: Ghost of Tsushima
summary: The wind as your compass, flower fields to the horizon and duels settled in a single strike.

title: Elden Ring
summary: An open world that doesn't hold your hand: behind every horizon there's a dungeon and a boss waiting.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
summary: Climb any wall, glide as far as the eye can see and solve things your way. Freedom turned into a mechanic.

title: Celeste
summary: Climbing the mountain is about anxiety and persistence. Precise dashes, generous checkpoints and a story that embraces you.

title: Hollow Knight
summary: Hand-drawn Hallownest, silence instead of a tutorial and a beautiful sadness at the back of every room.

title: Counter-Strike
summary: The LAN house routine: pay for the hour, pick terrorist or counter, and the "rush B" shout echoing through de_dust2.

title: Age of Empires II
summary: Villagers chopping wood, a battering ram pounding the wall and network matches running all night at the corner LAN house.
